title: On-prem deploy acceptance auditor and quota sanity checks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: As we ramp Private (VPC/on‑prem) adoption, customers frequently fail installs due to subtle environment mismatches: missing IAM permissions, exhausted quotas, DNS split‑horizon issues, or unavailable GPU SKUs. Our current preflight checks catch many cases but are brittle across cloud providers and air‑gapped on‑prem environments. This ticket scopes an "acceptance auditor" that runs preflight validations (quota projections, IAM/KMS checks, DNS resolvability, GPU SKU availability, network capacity) and emits actionable remediation guidance and remediation playbooks.

Goals:
- Provide a single CLI/API endpoint (rw-infra validate install) and a Terraform data-source that run provider-aware checks and return structured failures + recovery steps.
- Project required quota based on requested cluster topology (node counts, instance types, per-node GPUs, ENI counts) rather than check only current usage.
- Validate IAM principals and KMS/HSM policies used by Private control plane and node agents.
- Verify DNS resolution for private hosted zones, including conditional forwarders and split-horizon setups.
- Check GPU SKU availability using cloud quotas/offerings and allow a configurable SKU fallback list.
- Emit telemetry events and return deterministic exit codes for automation (0=ok, 1=warn, 2=fail).

Non-goals: full remediation automation (we provide remediation steps but won't auto-create quotas/roles). Deep hardware attestations for on‑prem hardware are out of scope for initial MVP.

Approach:
1) Define a canonical config model (json/yaml) to express target topology: region, AZ spread, node pools (count, instance type, GPUs per node, storage class), VPC CIDRs, expected NAT/IGW, expected route counts. This model will be consumed by both the CLI validator and a Terraform data source.
2) Implement provider adapters that translate checks into provider API calls (AWS, GCP, Azure) and a pluggable local mode for on‑prem/air‑gapped installs (runs prober scripts against given endpoints and local inventory).
3) Quota projection engine: given topology, compute required API quotas (vCPU, ENI, Elastic IPs, GPU count, IAM role limits) and compare to current limits; record shortfall and recommended request templates.
4) IAM & KMS validator: ensure control-plane roles exist, trust relationships are correct, and KMS key policies allow required Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey actions for service principals.
5) DNS validator: resolve control-plane hostname(s) from a bastion and from a customer-provided resolver; check split-horizon consistency and verify private hosted zone delegation and conditional forwarder rules.
6) GPU availability probe: query provider SKU catalogs and cross-check quotas; for on‑prem, validate GPU counts reported by node inventory (nvidia-smi or vendor API) and driver compatibility.
7) Produce machine-readable and human summaries, plus a remediation playbook with exact CLI snippets and Terraform HCL snippets for common fixes.

Outputs:
- rw-infra validate install --topology topology.yaml --> JSON result with checks[], remediation[], exit_code.
- Terraform data source rw_preflight_validation.topology -> accepts topology and returns validation_status and remediation_messages.
acceptance_criteria: CLI validator accepts topology.yaml and returns 0 when all checks pass for AWS, GCP, and Azure simulated testbeds.
Quota projection computes required vCPUs, ENIs, and GPU counts for a sample 50-node x 8 GPU deployment and lists any shortfalls with provider quota request templates.
IAM/KMS validator flags missing actions and returns step-by-step policy snippets for remediation (no ambiguous errors).
DNS validator detects split-horizon mismatches in a test harness and recommends route53/private hosted zone fixes or BIND forwarder entries.
GPU SKU availability check returns fallback candidates when preferred SKUs are out of quota and marks these as WARN instead of FAIL if allowed by topology config.
Terraform data source can be used in a plan to block apply when critical preflight checks fail (example in integration test).
Telemetry events created for each failed check with tags: provider, region, check_type, severity.
tasks: Design topology schema and open RFC (include optional fields for air-gapped mode)
Implement provider adapter interface and AWS/GCP initial adapters
Build quota projection engine and unit tests for vCPU/ENI/GPU calculations
Implement IAM/KMS validator using provider APIs and policy diffing
Write DNS prober that can run via bastion and direct resolver tests
Implement GPU SKU availability probe and on-prem inventory hooks
Add Terraform data source and integration tests that block plan/apply when critical failures occur
Create remediation playbook generator and a Confluence page with editable templates
Add telemetry + SLI for validator run success/failure rate and mean time to remediation
Docs + CLI examples + release notes for private-2026.03
updates: 2026-03-06 - Maya Chen: Kickoff RFC posted at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/On-prem+Acceptance+Auditor (draft). Seeking design review from infra-team and PM.
2026-03-08 - Samir Gupta: Spike completed for AWS quota APIs & prototype vCPU projection; documented edge-case where burstable instances count toward vCPU quota differently.
2026-03-10 - Leah Park (PM): Prioritized DNS split-horizon check after customer postmortem; added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12 - Samir Gupta: Prototype CLI returns structured JSON + exit codes. Found permissions gap: validator needs sts:AssumeRole with policy simulation in cross-account installs.
2026-03-14 - Engineering Review: Decided to ship Terraform data source as opt-in flag to avoid blocking existing CI for early adopters. Security will review KMS snippets next week.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-06): We should make remediation snippets copy-paste ready for both AWS CLI and Terraform. Avoid relying solely on console steps.
Samir Gupta (2026-03-08): For on‑prem mode, we'll accept an inventory JSON produced by the customer's installer; we'll validate GPU counts and driver versions from that inventory.
Leah Park (2026-03-11): Add customer-facing error codes so Support can quickly map a failed preflight run to a support flow.
Security (2026-03-14): Confirmed we'll not store persistent credentials during validation and will use short-lived tokens where possible. Full security review scheduled.
notes: Prefer fail-fast for critical capacity checks (GPU shortfall, missing IAM role) and warn for nonblocking items (DNS latency, suboptimal AZ spread).
Edge-case: provider returns 'soft limits' vs enforced quotas; map both to WARN/FAIL based on topology's strictness flag.
Consider integration with support toolchain: attach validator JSON output to support tickets with anonymized telemetry.
CLI design: --format json|yaml|human and --bastion-host flag to run resolver probes through customer bastion via SSH tunnel.
